God's Disdain
is a non-linear, traditional JRPG that began development in October of 2015.
The game is
free (no DRM/encryption)
for
Windows/Linux.
PLAY NOW:

/

/
NEWGROUNDS
STORY
The four nations of Hajimari have been struck with a plague that has put the entire island in peril. All plant life has slowly started to die away, causing conflict between the Grizz, Faerials, Komurans, and Haji. Many people have lost their lives not only to the plague, but wars between the nations as well. The islanders tried praying to the gods they worship, but received no answer. Many have given up, and many say the gods are dead.
All seemed hopeless, but sometimes hope can come from the most unsuspecting of spirits.
Tamiko and her brother Kenshin reside in the village of Komura on the southwest side of Hajimari. They've witnessed their family and friends die from the plague and other islanders which has compelled them to find the source of the plague and destroy it. They will meet friends and enemies alike on their journey, including the highly intelligent Locke, the child prodigy thief Avadel, the banished maniac Drago, and the powerful grandma Zeniba.
SCREENSHOTS/TRAILER
​
FEATURES
​
- Optional voice acting for the main story
- A unique EXP system that rewards actions rather than defeating enemies
- Hundreds of elemental armor and weapon combinations
- Open narrative design with a freely traversable world
- Unique and interesting side quests that build the world and setting
- A completely original soundtrack, sound effects included!
- Traditionally created paintings for story scenes
- Original art for all of the characters, enemies, and game icons
- A subtle karma system that affects the main character's personality
- Dynamic NPCs that follow their own schedule across four days in a day-night cycle
- 25+ hours of content
- Multiple endings

Version 1.0.13

Version 1.0.8

Version 1.0.7

-Fixed a softlock in Carivor Village.


Version 1.0.6

-Fixed a bug where a second boat would appear in the ocean if the player revived in a church after a death.

Version 1.0.5

-Changed some of Kenshin's text to better match his voice lines.

-Fixed a collision issue in Reikai.
-Fixed a bug with the Masahiro cutscene in Reikai that would prevent it from playing.

Insider Beta 1.4.0

This should help Rogue stand out a little bit more while also keeping the average damage output for a balanced party decent. 7% on Warrior might be too big of a hit but from my experience they deal the most damage typically so it shouldn't change too much.

In addition, I tried a different approach to updating the game this time. Instead of cooking up a whole new build, I just dragged the files over. If this works it will help updates be less tedious in the future. Let me know if you encounter any issues with files due to this.

The configuration file has reset, so please make sure to go into the options menu after loading your saved game and change them all to their previous values. This shouldn't happen again.

posts.author: Prescott
posts.body:
The image of success! I have completed my first FULL playthrough of God's Disdain. Along with the 27 hours of in-game time came over 200 hours of bug fixing, balance changes, and even overhauls of certain systems. It's still not perfect, but this is a major step for the game and one I am very happy to share with you all. This isn't a 100% playthrough, as I didn't finish/find around 15 quests and didn't enter a couple of dungeons. I also did the playthrough as a good character rather than an evil one, didn't have BGM on, or voice acting, so some bugs with those things might arise that need fixing as well. That's why the game isn't technically in beta just yet.
The next step for me is to get the remaining voice acting done, which entails re-recording all of Kenshin's dialogue and implementing another character's voice lines into the game. There have been some scheduling conflicts with Kenshin's VA as well as unfortunate events like sickness that have prevented us from getting it done for the past couple of months, but I am hopeful that it will get done soon.
In the meantime, I'll be working on getting a trailer made as well as a Steam page for the game. This has monetary costs to it as well, so it might take a little bit of time to ensure that I have the funds. As soon as I have the game's Steam page available, the game will be made available for everyone who worked on the game to test. This is not only to help further bug test the game, but also to figure out exactly how Steam works in terms of updating things for players so that I can hopefully get a better experience for when the beta comes. I've never used Steam as a developer before, so it will take some time to learn how to use it in a way that won't be obtuse for people who are trying to help out.
Once this testing is done, I should have a solid estimate for the release date. Then, I will announce a beta test that people may apply for, which will require a HacknPlan account. This beta will be focused on finding more bugs as well as making sure things are relatively balanced, but I won't be doing anything major to the game's systems or identity at this point. Once I feel that I've polished up as much as I can, and we're starting to see diminishing returns in terms of how many bugs are found versus how long the beta has been active, I'll close it and announce the true release date.
I am so, so excited to be at this stage of development! It's been a long time, nearly nine years since this project started, and being able to play through the game for the first time with all of the content intact was a magical experience for me. My goal was to hit 25-30 hours for a regular playthrough and it seems like I pretty much accomplished that! Of course, I'm the developer and I know this game very well so it'll likely take others a little bit longer to do the same amount of content, but even I was surprised by things in this game sometimes and I think that's the mark of something special.
It won't be much longer now. To all of those who I have talked about this project to for years, including the people who have worked on it, I hope that I can make you proud. To anybody who is learning about this project for the first time, I hope you find something here that will make you excited!

I played the newest version for a little over an hour, from the beginning, taking my time to check things out, and I stopped after talking to the lady quest giver after beating the first boss. Here are some additional thoughts.
As far as the mouse, it doesn't seem to work on the title screen. It seemed to work everywhere else, but it took me a while to figure out I could right click to exit or cancel things.
I discovered the keys used to scroll between party members in the menus, but only because I saw instructions for it in another game I tested. Instructions like that are very helpful. For instance, I don't think there is ever an instruction that tells the player that ESC will back out of a menu, but there are several menus where that is necessary. For instance, on the title screen. It is assumed that the player will know how to back out of the different options menus. Maybe everyone automatically knows that and I am just old.
As far as the class selection, as a player, in order to make an informed decision, it helps to know more about the differences and what, if any, skills might be useful in the game. If the differences between the classes is mostly stats, the ability to use magic, and a few special skills, then it may not make much of a difference. But then, as a player, I have to wonder what is different about the game play experience using the different classes and does it really matter.
About the sparkles to indicate something you can interact with, I would recommend putting something at the very beginning to demonstrate that this is a mechanic. That way a player like me who initially clicks on everything won't get frustrated or bored or just keep wondering if there is anything worth clicking on. And the map in one of the tents doesn't have the sparkles, but it seems like that would be the perfect place for it. Although I recommend putting a sparkling thing in the same space that the player first has autonomy to explore.
Takao is an NPC where you can finish the dialog under one menu option and then return directly to the choices selection, which is nice. Other NPCs don't have that same mechanic. This is also where I learned that the mouse wheel will scroll up and down in the list.
As a player, I would find it odd that the different level skills don't give any indication of how much different they are from other levels of that same skill. I have no idea what the difference is between Aqua 1, 2, 3, 4, etc. Only the highest level that says it hits all enemies shows any difference. For different levels of skills of the same type, I would expect more information about those different levels. This is the same for physical skills.
For the NPCs Tessera and Tommy, when you go to exit from a menu, you exit completely from the NPC dialog and have to initiate dialog again. In my opinion, it would be better for the dialog options to work like the Takao NPC.
In Dokutsu, I found a passability error. In the upper right corner of the map, after going up the ladder near Tessera's shop, if you keep going all the way up and to the right, you will find a point where you can walk onto the next "level" (steppe?) of the map. You can't really go anywhere up there. I think there are two squares accessible. But it looks odd to be able to walk over/through that square.
Something I noticed about combat. If you choose to Guard to regain HP/SP, but the last enemy is defeated that turn, whoever was Guarding doesn't regain any HP/SP. It seems like they should since that is one of the benefits of Guard.
I like the idea of actions versus defeating enemies increasing experience.
If I was supposed to find a small key somewhere before beating the boss, I didn't find it.
The monologue of the ??? NPC just confused me.
I'm not sure if I am supposed to go back to the cave and beat all the enemies again that respawned and if there is more to do in there. But I will check that out later.

Now, here are a few comments that are entirely based on personal preference. So please feel free to disregard them entirely. I will caveat these comments with saying that, as a player, I don't really enjoy games with super high numbers. High stats, damage, levels, etc. Which means that I am probably not the target audience for JRPG type games. Yes, I know it is ironic that I am learning to make games in RPG Maker. Anyway, for what it is worth:
I found the combat in the cave to be very repetitive and boring. I used the same options over and over without much challenge.
I felt that you gain levels much too quickly. But that might be normal for this type of game.
I noticed that you don't regain all SP when you gain a level, which may be intentional, but it made it so I couldn't use Kenshin's skills very often.
I noticed that you can't regain HP/SP outside of combat through like resting or something. At least I haven't seen a way yet. Other than through the items you find.
I'm the type of player that likes to find things. So not having things to click on and discover makes the game play a little boring. Because it seems like it is just reading and fighting. But I am still early in the game.
I honestly think it would be better to have some sort of battle back during combat. Maybe the enemy sprites don't look good on a battle back, but having just a blank, colored screen also looks a bit bland and uninteresting.
Tamiko's basic attack seems completely worthless at 10 damage.
I also feel like I fought quite a few enemies to not have enough currency to really buy anything in the way of equipment. I think I have maybe 140 something of the currency. Which doesn't buy much.
That is all I recall from playing and watching the video of my game play.
If you have any questions about any of these comments, just let me know. And again, feel free to disregard anything that shows that I don't know much about typical JRPG type games.

It sounds like you might still be in Komura. You need to leave in order to find places that progress the main story. Some NPCs will give you hints on how you can progress. Here are some things you can do:
Spoiler:
Leaving Komura solutions/hints
There is an NPC at the tavern in Sodai, the big city in Komura, that wears a wizard hat and sits in the corner. If you give her some Giku, she can give you a hint on what to do next.
You can travel to Grizz, the snowy region underneath Komura, by walking over a bridge and down through the mountains. The enemies are really strong here, so it might be best to try to avoid fighting. However, you can't complete either of the main quests in Grizz without the item obtained from the next hint.
There is a town on the left side of Komura next to a dock where you can do a quest for a boat. The boat will let you travel over to the other nations and other locations.
If you have managed to leave Komura, then my best advice is to just keep talking to everyone that you find. NPCs that can give you quests will do so as their default state, and they'll even often have zero changes to their schedule until they are activated by talking to them initially.
Spoiler:
Design philosophy
A lot of people may not be used to a game like this where there are no waypoints and no linear progression. It is great to have that freedom of adventure but it can get a little confusing in periods where you aren't sure what to do. The best thing to try is to just interact with everything you find! This is the way I've designed the game, for better or for worse depending on what kind of player you are. I wanted to focus a lot more on that feeling of exploration than being led on a linear path with a grand story. I often say that this game is "Dragon Quest meets Elder Scrolls" as an elevator pitch, and the latter's influence on the game is where the elements of exploration come in (leaning towards the Daggerfall/Morrowind style). Almost every single NPC has a name and a schedule and, if they don't have anything to give you in terms of quest lines, they do each have their own little stories that can be learned even if from only a few lines of dialogue.
I can totally understand if people don't like this kind of gameplay, I know a lot of people prefer their RPGs to be more linear experiences with the story and then have side quests along the path basically. It's just not really what I was going for. I will say, though, that I will definitely be doing that for my next RPG because what I've done here was way too large of an undertaking lol.
Either way I'm glad you have taken the time to test the game as much as you have. It's definitely been a big help!

It's been nearly a year since God's Disdain launched. It has progressed to the point that I feel it is finally deserving of that second decimal place going up!
Included in this are some bug fixes, but most notably also some new features:
Warriors can now use a Taunt skill to draw enemy aggression towards them. Warriors have high HP and can now use it to provide help to the rest of the party.
Rogues can now use a Steal skill to nab items off enemies without having to defeat them. Defeating enemies doesn't always result in drops, so this is a great way to get extra items.
If you have a Rogue in your party, you can now escape from most battles. Before, you could only escape from random battles on the overworld. Now, you can run around a dungeon stealing items from enemies and then safely retreating.
The desktop version of God's Disdain now also has the ability to export and import saves, so you can freely move saves between the desktop and web versions. You could always access the save files on the desktop version, but this will export a save in the web-friendly format for Newgrounds and Itch.io. Just remember that browser saves are somewhat volatile, so make sure to export your save slot before leaving the page.
I would love to hear feedback on how all of these features work. Let me know your thoughts!
